meta: John Opie's Street Singer and Child: a mother with a sleeping baby, shown by the Cleveland Museum as a sympathetic view of street life.
about: A woman in a grey bonnet and red shawl holds a sleeping child against her shoulder and looks off to one side. A folded printed sheet is tucked in the child's hand. John Opie came from a working-class family, and the Cleveland Museum says this made him sympathetic to labourers and led to an honest view of British street life. Street singers often sold goods too, but Opie leaves out any wares. The museum reads this as a way to make viewers see her humanity. She sings to feed her baby.
credit_line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. J. H. Wade

meta: Otto H. Bacher's 1893 painting July, a nude model on a sunlit lawn at East Hampton, with a curious story of a stolen truck.
about: A nude model sits on a lawn in strong sunlight. Otto Bacher, born in Cleveland and based in New York City, painted July during a visit to East Hampton on Long Island. Her name was not recorded. The Cleveland Museum adds an odd story. Several decades ago a man stole a truck that was carrying this painting, and police caught him about seven minutes later.

meta: David Johnson's 1851 oil study of a wild riverbed at North Conway, New Hampshire, with a guidebook's warning about the woods.
about: Angled boulders, slippery moss and splintered branches crowd this study of a riverbed at North Conway, New Hampshire, with dense undergrowth behind them. David Johnson painted it in 1851. The Cleveland Museum says his devotion to careful observation shows in the detail. North Conway was a popular starting point for tourists visiting the White Mountains. Guidebooks of the time warned about the dangers of the deep woods, and one compared wild forest-clambering to fighting a phalanx of porcupines.
credit_line: Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund

meta: Raphaelle Peale's miniature portrait of Robert Oliphant, a Philadelphia landowner's son who later vanishes from the record.
about: A man in a gray wig, a dark blue coat with gilt buttons and a white cravat tied with a blue ribbon is painted on an oval miniature in a gold frame. Robert Oliphant was the oldest son of William Oliphant, a wealthy Philadelphia landowner. His sister Elizabeth had her miniature painted by James Peale in 1795. Robert later moved to Norfolk, Virginia, and nothing more is known of him. Both miniatures descended in Elizabeth's family until a close family friend inherited them and bequeathed them to the museum.

meta: Giorgione's Holy Family, probably about 1500: Mary, the Child and Joseph, with a provenance that may reach back to Charles I.
about: The Virgin Mary sits on the ground in a blue mantle and rose dress holding the infant Christ, while an elderly Saint Joseph in a green robe leans toward them with a staff. The early ownership is uncertain. The National Gallery lists Charles I and James II of England as possible owners, and also the painter Allart van Everdingen, whose sale in Amsterdam in 1709 may have included it. A Brighton dealer sold it to Henry Willett in 1887. The Kress Foundation acquired it from Duveen Brothers in 1949.

meta: Abraham Hondius's The Adoration of the Shepherds, signed and dated 1663, a night Nativity with a woman carrying hens.
about: Mary and an angel kneel by the manger while shepherds crowd around. At the left a woman carries a cage of hens on her head beside a shepherd with a lantern, and at the right a small boy holds a basket of eggs. Angels on the clouds hold up a banderole. The Rijksmuseum records the panel as the pendant of another painting, and the painter signed and dated it on the fence at left in 1663. It was bought with the support of the Vereniging Rembrandt.

meta: Aertgen Claesz van Leyden's 1530 side panel of a triptych with a founder's wife kneeling beside Saint Catherine.
about: A crowned woman holds a sword beside a black-veiled figure who prays with a red rosary, in a hilly landscape with a castle. The Rijksmuseum says the praying woman is the founder's wife, kneeling in adoration and accompanied by Saint Catherine. This is the right wing of a triptych whose central panel shows the raising of Lazarus. Aertgen Claesz van Leyden dated it 1530. The left wing and the centre panel are catalogued with it in the Rijksmuseum.

meta: Bonaventura Peeters's 1640 coastal scene of seamen hunting polar bears, perhaps on the coast of Norway.
about: Seamen hunt polar bears on a mountainous rocky coast, perhaps off Norway, according to the Rijksmuseum. Two wooden huts stand at the foot of a mountain, and Dutch warships lie out at sea. A small rowing boat carries the painter's initials BP. Bonaventura Peeters dated the picture 1640. It belonged to F. Poupe Serrane in Brussels, from whom the museum bought it in 1910, and it was later lent to the Scheepvaartmuseum in Amsterdam.

meta: A six-panel screen with painted fans scattered over a darkened silver river, catalogued under Hon'ami Koetsu in the Freer Gallery.
about: Painted fans seem to be scattered across a river of silver, which has darkened over time to nearly black. The museum says screens of this type recall a story of a prince crossing a bridge in Kyoto. He tossed his fan into the river, and his companions followed, admiring the fans as they fluttered toward the water. Many such screens came from the Tawaraya atelier headed by Sotatsu. The museum finds the shape, colour and soft outlines of the rocks comparable to the islands in Sotatsu's Waves at Matsushima screens.

meta: Juan de Flandes's The Birth and Naming of John the Baptist, from an altarpiece for Queen Isabella I of Castile, 1496 to 1499.
about: Elizabeth rests in a green canopy bed after labour while the Virgin Mary presents the newborn to his father, Zacharias. He writes the baby's name on a scroll. He had lost his speech when he doubted an angel's prophecy, and at this moment it returns. The room suggests a comfortable Netherlandish home, with a brazier at lower right and a concave mirror above the bed. Juan de Flandes painted it between 1496 and 1499 for an altarpiece commissioned by Queen Isabella I of Castile for a monastery near Burgos.

meta: Jean-Charles-Joseph Rémond's Mountain Landscape with Road to Naples, about 1821 to 1825: sunlight in a deep valley above a river.
about: Sunlight pours into a deep valley, running over rock and down a green hillside to a bend in the river far below. At the left a steep rock face rises over a group of travellers on a narrow mountain road, and buildings sit high on the cliff beyond. The Getty says Rémond was widely known for his Italian landscapes, especially oil studies prized for their light and fluid handling. He won the Prix de Rome for landscape in 1821. In Rome he travelled widely, including to Naples.

meta: Nicoletto da Modena's engraved ornament panel inscribed Victoria Augusta, with Apollo and Marsyas and satyrs, about 1500.
about: The upper part of this print shows the musical contest between Apollo with his lyre and Marsyas with bagpipes. Below, in a narrow relief, Marsyas is flayed. Two satyrs sit playing pipes on a pedestal at the bottom, and in the relief above them a satyr pipes to a stag while Apollo chases Daphne. Banners at the top carry the inscription Victoria Augusta. The museum describes the whole image as heavily ornamented with figures. Nicoletto da Modena made the engraving about 1500.

meta: David Teniers's Landscape with Peasants Dancing, about 1645 to 1650: villagers dance to a bagpiper outside a rustic inn.
about: Villagers talk and dance to a bagpiper's tune in front of a thatched inn, with a turreted stone house on a grassy rise at the right. David Teniers painted it about 1645 to 1650. The Cleveland Museum places him among Netherlandish artists whose pictures celebrate country life. Such delicately painted works, it says, were made mainly for an elite urban audience nostalgic for a simpler existence. This one combines two of his specialties, landscape and scenes of country life.
credit_line: Gift of the Frances W. Ingalls Trust
